circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi that was designed by Hermann Tilke and has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The circuit represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One venues, following Bahrain and preceding circuits in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street-based motorsport venue located around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside supporting racing championships. The track holds FIA Grade 1 status and serves as a premier racing destination in Australia.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the Austrian Grand Prix venue throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following its reconstruction and renaming, the track resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital that spans 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One racing. The circuit first hosted a grand prix in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the 5. 412 km Bahrain International Circuit serves as home to the region's premier motorsport events, most notably hosting the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, which marked the Middle East's inaugural F1 race. The venue accommodates various racing series including drag racing and endurance competitions, and previously featured Australian V8 Supercars before their departure after 2010, while maintaining FIA Grade 1 certification with multiple configurable track layouts.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it representative of modern circuit design. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The Spa-Francorchamps circuit in Belgium stretches 7. 004 km and has been a fixture of international motorsport since 1925, becoming part of Formula One from the sport's inaugural season in 1950. Now hosting the Belgian Grand Prix, this legendary venue has maintained an annual F1 presence since 1985, with only two absences in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary street circuit that serves as the home of the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track has accommodated various international racing series including sportscar championships and North American open-wheel competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit hosted China's Formula One grand prix annually from 2004 until 2019, with the event resuming from 2024. The venue has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing competitions alongside its primary Formula One commitment.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, England, this circuit hosted the inaugural 1948 British Grand Prix and later the 1950 race that launched the World Championship of Drivers. After alternating with Aintree and Brands Hatch for three decades, the British Grand Prix found its permanent home here from 1987 onwards, and the venue continues to host major motorcycle racing events.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km circuit located near Budapest in Hungary, hosted the sport's first grand prix held in a communist-controlled nation when it opened in 1986. Built in just eight months, faster than any other Formula One venue, the track was constructed outside the city near a major highway after the government rejected plans for a street circuit in Budapest's largest park.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit located near Milan in northern Italy, constructed in 1922 as the third purpose-built racing venue globally and Europe's oldest on the mainland. Home to the Italian Grand Prix continuously since 1949 (except during 1980 renovations), the track earned its "Temple of Speed" nickname through its characteristic long straights and fast-corner layout.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Located in Mie Prefecture, Japan, the Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807-kilometer track operated by Honda Mobilityland that serves as a premier venue for top-tier motorsport competition. The facility regularly hosts both the Formula One World Championship and Japanese Super Formula races, and can accommodate up to 155,000 spectators.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course located in Paradise, Nevada, that weaves through the famous Las Vegas Boulevard, showcasing iconic venues such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas. The track utilizes the city's main entertainment district, featuring the prominent hotels and casinos that define the region's landscape.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: This 4. 3-kilometre Mexico City venue is named in honour of brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both of whom died in racing accidents during the 1960s. The track has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix twice before, most recently in 1992, and returned to the calendar in 2015 with a revised layout.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, spanning 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and an average qualifying speed of approximately 139 mph. Designed by specialist circuit architects Apex Circuit Design, the venue hosts the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track winding through the urban streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, circling the harbour in the Principality of Monaco. Though officially recognized by both names, it is predominantly called "Monte Carlo" after the neighbourhood that encompasses most of the circuit.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch dunes near the North Sea and west of Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix following its Formula One return in 2021. The venue will conclude its F1 partnership after the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Lusail International Circuit, situated near Lusail north of Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419-kilometer motorsport venue featuring a 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing circuit in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate late Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who tragically died in an aircraft accident eight years prior. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features associated karting facilities.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street circuit located along the Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, that has hosted the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since 2021 and recently began hosting a Formula E event. The venue combines urban racing with coastal scenery on the corniche promenade.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown waterfront district, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang planning zones as it traces a path around the bay itself.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Montmeló, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas spans 3. 426 miles and meets the highest FIA standards for international racing. The venue currently hosts Formula One's United States Grand Prix alongside major motorcycle and endurance racing series, while previously welcoming various touring car, rallycross, and sports car competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British driver who currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: The Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships (2005-2006 with Renault) and 32 Grand Prix victories over 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, winning the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, two Le Mans 24-hour races, and the 2019 Daytona 24-hour event, making him the sole driver to have won both a Formula One drivers' title and the world sportscar championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian racing driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined Mercedes on the Formula One grid in 2025 and has since secured six Grand Prix victories for the team.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabriel Bortoleto currently races in Formula One for Audi, competing at the sport's highest level in this latest chapter of his motorsport career.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 13-season career that includes 10 Grand Prix victories. He achieved runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during consecutive seasons at Mercedes, finishing second in both 2019 and 2020.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine driver Franco Alejandro Colapinto currently races in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian racing driver Jack Doohan competes in endurance racing while holding a reserve role at Haas in Formula One, where he has participated in seven Grand Prix events during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri stands as a notable achievement in his racing career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar, representing France in Formula One, currently races for Red Bull Racing. The French and Algerian driver continues to pursue his career in the sport's premier category.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: British racing driver Lewis Hamilton currently competes for Ferrari in Formula One. He has claimed seven world championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record, while also holding numerous other records including the most career victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg, a German driver, currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved success in sports car racing, securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor who currently drives for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Monaco-born Charles Leclerc races for Ferrari in Formula One, having secured second place in the championship standings during 2022. The driver has claimed nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: K-Mag is a Danish racing driver who last competed in Formula One through 2024, having previously raced in the sport from 2014 to 2020. Currently, he focuses on the FIA World Endurance Championship driving for BMW through WRT, while also taking on a part-time NASCAR role with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently competing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with the team. Throughout his eight seasons in the sport, he has secured 12 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The driver previously achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez, known as "Checo," currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after spending 15 seasons in the sport. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has accumulated six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver, races for McLaren in Formula One and has claimed nine Grand Prix victories during his four-year career in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: An Australian driver who raced in Formula One between 2011 and 2024, Daniel Ricciardo earned the nickname "the Honey Badger" during his 14-season career. He secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has claimed seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-year career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four race victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery in IMSA competition for Era Motorsports.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently competing for Aston Martin.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently serving as reserve for Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls following his Formula One career that spanned from 2021 through 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing and has dominated Formula One with four consecutive world championship titles spanning 2021 to 2024. Across his 12-season career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories, establishing himself as one of the sport's most successful drivers.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor to date, raced in the series from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. He continues his involvement in the sport in a support capacity for the American team.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has operated under the Alpine banner since 2021, serving as Renault's works operation until the manufacturer's departure at the end of 2025, and competes using Mercedes powerplants. Alpine's only victory came through Esteban Ocon at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, with the squad previously racing as Renault F1 Team and drawing its engine supply from Mercedes during its earlier Lotus era in 2015.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has entered Formula One multiple times throughout its history, with the current iteration operating under AMR GP Limited and competing under the Aston Martin Aramco branding in the championship.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: The Scuderia Ferrari racing division competes in Formula One as the sport's longest-running and most accomplished team, participating in every World Championship since its inception in 1950. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" after their iconic emblem, the Italian outfit represents the racing heritage of Ferrari.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas, the squad commenced competition in 2016 after its establishment in 2014. Ayao Komatsu currently leads the team as principal, taking over from Guenther Steiner who held the position since the team's launch until stepping down in early 2024.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering firm established itself through endurance racing success, including a Le Mans victory in 1989, before joining Formula One in 1993 as an independent constructor. The team competed in the sport for over three decades, becoming the fourth-longest-serving chassis manufacturer by race entries before ceasing operations in 2025, when its operations and infrastructure were acquired by Audi to serve as the foundation for the manufacturer's F1 program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under Mastercard sponsorship. The team operates as part of the McLaren Group, which is owned by Bahrain's Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One continuously since 1954, initially as an engine supplier and later as a full team operator. The current iteration, based in Brackley and operating under a German licence, features a tripartite ownership structure established in 2022 involving Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff. The team is colloquially known as the "Silver Arrows" due to its traditional livery.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor established in 2024, operating as the second team within the Red Bull organization alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull GmbH's dual-team strategy in the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced racing in 2024 as one of two Red Bull-owned squads alongside Red Bull Racing. Operating from Faenza with a satellite facility near Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull's second constructor in the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed team headquartered in England, has been one of Red Bull GmbH's two Formula One entries since its establishment in 2005. Christian Horner led the team through its entire two-decade history until 2025, when Laurent Mekies took over as team principal.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's previous failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in the 2026 season as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and operates from a substantial purpose-built facility.
